text.home.introTitle:
Tattoo artist by trade.
*Free soul* by nature.
text.home.introText: I tattoo black & grey realism and travel with the machine — Amsterdam, Phuket, Portugal and wherever the road goes next. Life is meant to be lived, so I live it my way: making work that lasts, meeting people who leave a mark, and giving something back.
text.home.journalText: Words from the road — the people, the places and the lessons in between.
text.home.craftText: In black & grey, every highlight is skin left untouched — so the shadows have to do all the talking.
text.home.soulText: It don't cost a thing to care. The Last Soul is my long-term project to help children in need, vulnerable people, families and communities — and it started with one man in Thailand.
text.about.title:
Ângelo
Salavessa
text.about.statement: Realism is a discipline of *restraint* — knowing where not to put ink.
text.about.p1: I work in black & grey realism — faces, animals, roses, statues and symbols, rendered in soft gradients that sit naturally on the body.
text.about.p2: I work on the road. Amsterdam, Phuket and Portugal are regular stops, and the work goes wherever I land next.
text.about.p3: Nothing was ever handed to me, and I'm grateful for that. I had to find positivity while facing a lot of negativity — it's part of my process. It's not easy to be an artist, but it's the most beautiful path I have, and the one I enjoy the most.
text.about.quote: I've always realised that life is meant to be lived — so let it be my way.
text.about.quotePt: “Sempre percebi que a vida é para ser vivida, então que seja à minha maneira.”
text.about.words: The greatness of a man is not in how much wealth he acquires, but in his integrity and his ability to affect those around him positively.

Be kind.

text.soul.lead: The Last Soul is my long-term project to help people — children in need, vulnerable people, families and communities. I want to use my work, my brand, my business relationships and my network to create opportunities to help as many people as possible.
text.soul.missionTitle:
It don't cost a thing
to *care.*
text.soul.missionText: A word, a smile, a little love. That's how we evolve. We learn. We teach.
text.soul.missionText2: Sometimes people don't need much. A little attention, a helping hand, some food or medicine — or simply someone who cares. The Last Soul exists to make sure more of them get it.
text.soul.storyText: I met Papa four years ago in Thailand. He's one of those people who leave a mark on you without even realising it. When I heard he'd crashed his bike, I went to see him, spend some time together and make sure he was okay.
text.soul.storyQuote: Let's remind someone that they're not alone.
text.soul.initText: Every initiative is real, specific and personal. They'll be listed here as they happen.
text.soul.involvedText: No pressure, no expectations. Every little bit of kindness counts.
text.soul.way1Text: Even €2 or €5 can help — food, medicine, or whatever someone needs most. Text me and you're part of the plan.
text.soul.way2Text: Brands, studios and companies who want to help: let's talk about what we can build together.
text.soul.way3Text: Tell someone's story. Share the project. Remind someone they're not alone.
text.soul.futureText: The Last Soul is built to grow — from one act of kindness into a platform for initiatives, partners and stories from around the world. This page will grow with it.

process.title: The message
process.text: Send the idea, the placement, a rough size and any references. Short is fine. The form below turns it into one clear WhatsApp message.

process.title: The conversation
process.text: What will actually work on your body: scale, flow, where the light falls on the muscle. Realism needs room — sometimes the honest answer is bigger, or simpler.

process.title: The design
process.text: The composition is built for you and your placement. Dates, deposits and session length are agreed directly when you book.

process.title: The session
process.text: Black & grey is built in layers — from the deepest shadow up to the highlights. Large pieces are split across sessions. To be continued.

process.title: The healing
process.text: Follow the aftercare you're given. Healed realism softens and settles into the skin — that's the version you live with, and the one that counts.

journal.title: Papa
journal.excerpt: Sometimes people don't need much. A little attention, a helping hand, some food or medicine — or simply someone who cares.
journal.body:
Yesterday, I found out that Papa had crashed his bike. I met him four years ago here in Thailand, and he's one of those people who leave a mark on you without even realising it.

When I heard what had happened, I decided to visit him, spend some time together and make sure he was doing okay.

It reminded me of something important: sometimes, people don't need much. A little attention, a helping hand, some food or medicine, or simply someone who cares.

I want to share more of Papa's story and how our paths crossed years ago. And I'd love to do something more for him. If you'd like to be part of this little initiative, even €2 or €5 could help us get him some food, medicine or anything else he might need. No pressure, no expectations. Every little bit of kindness counts.

Let's remind someone that they're not alone. If you want to be part of the plan, just text me.

> Be kind. It's gangster.

journal.title: Borrowed love
journal.excerpt: Some kinds of love are borrowed. We don't own them — we just get to experience them.
journal.body:
Sometimes love arrives in the smallest, sweetest ways, like a sandy little heartbeat you meet by the ocean. For a moment, the world slows down. You hold this tiny life in your hands and it feels like love has chosen you. Not forever, just for now. And that “now” is enough.

Some kinds of love are borrowed like that. We don't own them. We just get to experience them — the warmth, the trust, the softness resting against our chest. One day it changes, like the tide. But its purpose was never to stay. Its purpose was to remind us what tenderness feels like.

So we honour the love we cross paths with, even if it's just for one golden afternoon on the beach with a little dog who made the world feel gentle again.

> What truly remains is not the love we keep, but the love we learn.

journal.title: To lose ourselves, to find ourselves

journal.body:
Just an island boy trying to make it.

> We travel, initially, to lose ourselves; and we travel, next, to find ourselves. We travel to open our hearts and eyes and learn more about the world than our newspapers will accommodate.

— Pico Iyer

Let's get it.

journal.title: A free soul
journal.excerpt: It wasn't the easiest year — but perhaps the one with the most learning.
journal.source: Originally shared on Instagram, in Portuguese and English.
journal.body:
I want to thank everyone for their support this year. It wasn't the easiest, but perhaps the one with the most learning, the most baggage, and some notion of what I want — and even more of what I don't want.

I've never been one to have anything easy, and thank goodness. I wasn't born into a rich family, and thank goodness. I had to find some positivity while facing a lot of negativity, but it's part of my process, and thank goodness.

It's not easy to be an artist, but it's the most beautiful path I have and the one I enjoy the most. I am a free soul, and these achievements were all personal, in favour of that.

> I've always realised that life is meant to be lived, so let it be my way.

I wish everyone twice as much as they wish me. To my people: the top feels better when we all get there together. Let's get it.

*“Sempre percebi que a vida é para ser vivida, então que seja à minha maneira.”*
